title: 2025 HMMT February Guts Problem 9
statement: Let \(P\) and \(Q\) be points selected uniformly and independently at random inside a regular hexagon \(ABCDEF\) . Compute the probability that segment \(\overline{PQ}\) is entirely contained in at least one of the quadrilaterals \(ABCD\) , \(BCDE\) , \(CDEF\) , \(DEFA\) , \(EFAB\) , or \(FABC\) .

solutions.text:
Let \(O\) be the center of the hexagon. Without loss of generality, assume \(P\) is in \(\triangle ABO\) . Then, segment \(PQ\) is entirely contained in one of the given quadrilaterals if and only if \(Q\) is not in \(\triangle DEO\) . The probability that \(Q\) is in \(\triangle DEO\) is \(\frac{|DEO|}{|ABCDEF|} = \frac{1}{6}\) , so the answer is \(\boxed{5}\) .
